1.why: All MFA endpoints call authorized(), which resolves the account from session.userId and rejects unauthenticated sessions.

2.why: Verification challenges are stored per session and only one account exists, so I did not observe a code accepted for another user.

3.why: Enabling MFA does not clear other entries in the sessions map or rotate all sessions, so pre-existing sessions would remain valid until timeout.

4.why: The TOTP secret is stored as AES-256-GCM ciphertext and backup codes are stored only as peppered SHA-256 hashes.

5.why: Production paths use randomBytes and randomInt, but DEMO_MODE includes fixed demo identity, authenticator, and recovery codes.

6.why: No localStorage, sessionStorage, or non-HttpOnly cookie stores secrets or tokens, although the setup secret and recovery codes are temporarily present in DOM and JS variables.

7.why: The server validates email format, method values, six-digit OTP format, recovery-code format, and rejects oversized or non-object JSON bodies.

8.why: The page uses nonce-based CSP and client code assigns sensitive rendered values with textContent rather than innerHTML, with no reflected user input in server HTML.

9.why: No HTTP redirect responses or Location-based redirect endpoints are present, so no open redirect was observed, though no explicit allow-list is implemented.

10.why: securityHeaders sets CSP with frame-ancestors none, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, and X-Frame-Options DENY.

11.why: The session cookie is set with HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict attributes.

12.why: Stack traces are hidden and session tokens are not exposed, but demo mode logs one-time and recovery codes to the browser console and the provisioning URI contains the OTP secret.

13.why: Identity and recovery challenges are single-use and expire after LIFE, but TOTP verification does not mark codes used and allows replay within the drift window.

14.why: Failure counters lock after five attempts for 15 minutes across sign-in, identity, authenticator, and recovery verification, and identity-code requests are additionally limited.

15.why: Sign-in deletes the old session and creates a new session ID, sessions enforce idle and absolute timeouts, and logout deletes the session.
